data.description:
## Context / Problem

A ticket directory containing NO events — created by a write that never emitted its CREATE event —
makes the plan-relation reducer error out, and that error surfaces as an INDETERMINATE verdict on
plan reviews of OTHER, UNRELATED tickets. The blast radius is every ticket whose relation graph the
snapshot walks, which in practice means an entire epic.

## Reproduced, then fixed, by removing the directory and nothing else

Running `rebar review-plan 5267-f026-0f2b-4c02`:

    verdict INDETERMINATE, exit 2, llm_ran: FALSE
    indeterminate[0] = {id: plan-relation-snapshot-error, reason: reducer-error,
                        canonical_id: None, reference: 0de5-6db1-8058-4e80}
    ERROR rebar.llm.plan_review: plan relation snapshot failed

`0de5-6db1-8058-4e80` was an EMPTY DIRECTORY in `.tickets-tracker` — `ls -A` returned 0 entries,
`rebar show` reported `has no CREATE or SNAPSHOT event`. A second one, `4ab3-411d-9736-4a41`, was in
the same state.

CRITICALLY, 5267 DOES NOT REFERENCE 0de5. Its only dep is `relates_to 208f-6e90-1326-403a`; the
broken directory was reached by walking the epic's relation graph. A grep across the whole store for
`0de5-6db1-8058-4e80` returned ZERO references from any ticket — nothing points at it at all.

After removing the two empty directories and changing nothing else, the SAME command on the SAME tree
returned `verdict: PASS`, exit 0, attestation certified at ff295b9cf87. That is the causal proof: one
variable changed.

## Why this is worth fixing rather than sweeping

* It is NOT transient. An earlier agent on this epic hit the same signature and recorded it as
  "transient store churn from a half-written ticket, retried clean". It is not churn — it persists
  until someone removes the directory, and a retry only appears to work if the racing writer happens
  to complete in the interim.
* The error names the BROKEN ticket, not the one being reviewed, so the failure looks like a problem
  with an unrelated ticket. That is a strong wrong-direction signal for anyone debugging it.
* It is invisible to git. Git cannot track empty directories, so the artifact never appears in
  `git status`, never reaches the tickets branch, and cannot be spotted by inspecting the shared
  history — it exists only in a local clone.
* The LLM never runs (`llm_ran: false`), so the gate fails closed with no spend. That is correct
  behaviour, but it means the whole epic's claims and closes stall on a filesystem artifact.

## Approach (not yet decided)

The reducer should tolerate a ticket directory with no CREATE/SNAPSHOT event rather than failing the
whole snapshot — most plausibly by skipping it with a warning naming the path, since a directory with
no events carries no information that a relation snapshot needs. Consider also whether the writer can
avoid creating the directory before it has an event to put in it, which would remove the artifact at
source.

Both directions should be weighed; tolerating the artifact is the smaller, safer change and fixes
existing broken clones, while fixing the writer prevents new ones and does nothing for clones already
carrying one.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A ticket directory with no CREATE/SNAPSHOT event does not fail the plan-relation snapshot; the
      review proceeds and the artifact is reported as a warning naming the offending path.
- [ ] A test constructs an event-less ticket directory and asserts `review-plan` on an UNRELATED
      ticket still reaches a verdict; it fails before the fix.
- [ ] It is decided and recorded whether the writer should also stop creating the directory before it
      has an event to write, with the reasoning either way.
- [ ] make lint and make typecheck pass by exit code; the default selection is green.
data.title: An event-less ticket directory fails the plan-relation reducer, turning unrelated plan reviews INDETERMINATE
